Chapter 4: Finding a Voice—From Survivor to Advocate on the World Stage
Coming out of the shadows of trauma, some survivors find themselves drawn to a new purpose. That pain they’ve carried? It turns into fuel for something bigger—the drive to make sure what happened to the Yazidis is never forgotten, and that others are protected from suffering a similar fate.
Speaking out isn’t an easy decision. Imagine having to relive your worst memories in front of strangers, facing their doubts or even hostility, and risking more pain. But for those who choose this path, the impact can be life-changing.
Picture this: the first time a survivor stands up to speak, their fear is almost overwhelming. Words come slowly, weighed down by emotion and the heaviness of memory. But as the story unfolds, something shifts. The listeners are drawn in—and the speaker begins to realize their voice has real power. That silence, the one that once surrounded the Yazidi tragedy, starts to break.
Traveling to far-off countries, meeting politicians, activists, and journalists, the survivor becomes a symbol of resilience. Their personal story turns abstract headlines into something real—something you can feel. When they sit down with world leaders, the message is simple but urgent: what happened to the Yazidis isn’t just a tragedy for one group—it’s a warning to everyone.
Advocacy can look very different from person to person. Some focus on raising awareness, sharing their stories in schools, at conferences, or through the media. Others roll up their sleeves and help fellow survivors find medical care, education, or legal support. The fight against sexual violence and human trafficking becomes central, as survivors demand better protection for vulnerable communities and tougher action against those who exploit them.
Of course, there are setbacks. Promises get made and broken, and change often comes at a crawl. But there are moments of hope too—a new law passes, a perpetrator faces justice, or a survivor finds healing by supporting others. The work is exhausting, but there’s a powerful sense of purpose that keeps them going.
Picture a survivor, sitting alone after a long day of meetings. The pain is still there, but so is pride. What was once a source of shame has turned into a tool for change. The fight isn’t over, not by a long shot—but knowing that even one voice can make a difference brings comfort.
Most of us probably underestimate the power of testimony. It’s easy to look away from stories of suffering, to believe there’s nothing we can do. But when survivors speak up, the world can’t help but listen. The struggle for justice and recognition is ongoing, but every story told is a step closer to a future where these kinds of atrocities become impossible.
